process_area.title: Leakage Recovery, Revenue Analytics & Continuous Assurance

value_stream.name: Revenue Assurance, Pricing Integrity & Leakage Management

fields.Participants: Revenue Assurance Lead, BI (links to VS-28.1), Finance (links to VS-17.4), POS/IT (links to VS-08/VS-27), Channel owners (VS-10/VS-13/VS-54/VS-58/VS-80/VS-95), Loss Prevention (links to VS-23)
fields.Trigger: Exception alert (W3693); reconciliation variance (W3691/W3694); integrity anomaly

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-monitor of "Revenue Assurance Lead/BI triage and investigate exceptions from the" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-route of "route the leakage" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-585 (ensure controlled execution — Leakage Recovery, Revenue Analytics & Continuous Assurance (PA-118.3).)
- operational: continuous monitoring; operational: structured quantification method
Pain Points / Risks: - **Detection-latency risk**: Leakage persists undetected for long periods; mitigated by continuous monitoring
- **Quantification-error risk**: Leakage impact mis-estimated; mitigated by structured quantification method
System Touchpoints: - Exception monitors (links to W3693/W3697–W3704); BI/analytics (links to VS-28.1); channel systems (VS-08/VS-10/VS-13/VS-54/VS-58/VS-80/VS-95); loss prevention (links to VS-23)

steps.activity: Revenue Assurance Lead/BI triage and investigate exceptions from the integrity monitors (W3697–W3704): classify each by leakage vector (W3690), determine whether it represents genuine leakage, and prioritize by value/volume/risk

Revenue Assurance Lead quantify confirmed leakage: estimate the revenue impact (rate × volume × period), determine root cause (system defect, process gap, master-data error, human error, fraud), and assess the control failure (W3693)
steps.r: Revenue Assurance Lead / BI / Channel owner

steps.activity: Revenue Assurance Lead route the leakage: fraud/collusion to investigation (W3708), recoverable to recovery (W3706), system/process root-cause to corrective action, and feed all to analytics (W3707) and the channel owner for fix

fields.Participants: Revenue Assurance Lead, Finance (links to VS-17.1), Channel owners, Customer Service (links to VS-13), Payments (links to VS-80), IT (links to VS-27.1), Audit (links to VS-21.3)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-document of "document the event in the leakage register" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-585 (ensure controlled execution — Leakage Recovery, Revenue Analytics & Continuous Assurance (PA-118.3).)
- operational: prevention focus; operational: corrective-action verification
Pain Points / Risks: - **Non-recovery risk**: Leakage identified but not recoverable (e.g., customer already left); mitigated by prevention focus
- **Recurrence risk**: Root cause not fixed, leakage recurs; mitigated by corrective-action verification
System Touchpoints: - Finance/GL (links to VS-17.1); IT service mgmt (links to VS-27.1); master data (links to W3709/VS-29); controls (links to W3693); audit (links to VS-21.3); leakage register (links to W3696)

steps.activity: Revenue Assurance Lead/Finance recover leakage where recoverable: re-charge under-charged transactions where identifiable, recover over-refunded/erroneous value, pursue third-party (acquirer/vendor) recovery for fee/chargeback discrepancies, and correct GL entries (links to VS-17.1)
steps.r: Revenue Assurance Lead / Finance / Channel owner

steps.activity: Revenue Assurance Lead drive corrective action on root cause: system fix (with IT links to VS-27.1), process change, master-data correction (W3709), control addition/tuning (W3693), and training to prevent recurrence
steps.r: Revenue Assurance Lead / IT / Channel owner

steps.activity: Revenue Assurance Lead/Audit verify recovery and corrective-action effectiveness: confirm leakage stopped, recovery captured, control now detects it, and document the event in the leakage register; report to analytics (W3707) and audit (links to VS-21.3)

fields.Participants: Revenue Assurance Lead, BI (links to VS-28.1), Finance/FP&A (links to VS-17.4), Audit (links to VS-21.3), Channel owners, Governance (links to VS-36)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-analyze of "analyze leakage trends" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-forecast of "Revenue Assurance Lead publish analytics to FP&A" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-585 (ensure controlled execution — Leakage Recovery, Revenue Analytics & Continuous Assurance (PA-118.3).)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Metric-blindness risk**: No visibility into leakage trends; mitigated by KPI dashboard
- **Benchmark-gap risk**: Leakage rate unknown vs industry; mitigated by benchmarking
System Touchpoints: - BI/analytics (links to VS-28.1); FP&A (links to VS-17.4); audit (links to VS-21.3); governance (links to VS-36); program governance (links to W3689)

steps.activity: Revenue Assurance Lead/BI maintain the revenue-assurance KPI dashboard: leakage rate by channel/vector, leakage value recovered vs unrecovered, control-firing/effectiveness, exception-cycle-time, reconciliation integrity, and program maturity

Revenue Assurance Lead analyze leakage trends: by channel, vector, store, cashier, time-period; identify systemic vs isolated issues, control-effectiveness decay, and emerging new leakage patterns; benchmark leakage rate vs retail norms (1–3%)

Revenue Assurance Lead publish analytics to FP&A (links to VS-17.4 — revenue-forecast/leakage adjustment), channel owners (for fix prioritization), audit (links to VS-21.3), and governance (links to W3689/VS-36); drive the leakage-reduction target

fields.Participants: Revenue Assurance Lead, Loss Prevention (links to VS-23), Internal Audit (links to VS-21.3), Legal (links to VS-100.3), HR (links to VS-19), Channel owners, POS/IT (links to VS-08/VS-27.3)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-flag for investigation of "investigate revenue-loss fraud/collusion/abuse" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System workflow orchestration of "coordinate with internal audit" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-report of "report fraud-loss exposure to governance" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-585 (ensure controlled execution — Leakage Recovery, Revenue Analytics & Continuous Assurance (PA-118.3).)
- operational: exception analytics and CCTV correlation; operational: prevention and control-hardening
Pain Points / Risks: - **Undetected-collusion risk**: Cashier-customer collusion hard to detect; mitigated by exception analytics and CCTV correlation
- **Recovery-difficulty risk**: Stolen value hard to recover; mitigated by prevention and control-hardening
System Touchpoints: - Loss prevention (links to VS-23); exception monitoring (links to W837/W841/W1475/W1476); CCTV (links to VS-23.2); audit (links to VS-21.3); legal (links to VS-100.3); HR (links to VS-19/VS-84)

steps.activity: Revenue Assurance Lead/Loss Prevention investigate revenue-loss fraud/collusion/abuse: cashier-customer sweethearting, refund/void fraud (links to W841), coupon/promo abuse (links to W1475), gift-card fraud (links to W1476), loyalty-points manipulation, pricing/override collusion, and external payment/chargeback fraud; gather transaction/ CCTV/ system evidence
steps.r: Revenue Assurance Lead / Loss Prevention / Audit

steps.activity: Revenue Assurance Lead/Loss Prevention/HR manage confirmed fraud: employee-disciplinary/legal action (links to VS-19/VS-84/VS-100), customer/law-enforcement escalation, recovery of stolen value, and control-hardening to prevent recurrence; coordinate with internal audit (links to VS-21.3)
steps.r: Revenue Assurance Lead / Loss Prevention / HR / Legal

steps.activity: Revenue Assurance Lead quantify fraud-loss and recovery, feed the event to loss-prevention analytics (links to VS-23.3/W845) and audit (links to VS-21.3), and report fraud-loss exposure to governance (links to W3689/VS-36) and the risk committee (links to VS-21.2)

fields.Participants: Revenue Assurance Lead, MDM (links to VS-29), Merchandising/Pricing (links to VS-01.2), POS/IT (links to VS-08/VS-27), Tax (links to VS-79), Promotions (links to VS-58), BI (links to VS-28.1)
fields.Trigger: Leakage root cause = master-data/system defect; data-governance cycle

workflows.name: Pricing & Promo System Governance & Master-Data Integrity

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-validate of "verify price master accuracy" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System rule-based authorization of "unauthorized/manual price changes that cause leakage" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-monitor of "monitor master-data quality KPIs" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-585 (ensure controlled execution — Leakage Recovery, Revenue Analytics & Continuous Assurance (PA-118.3).)
- operational: data-integrity monitoring; operational: change governance
Pain Points / Risks: - **Master-data-defect risk**: Wrong price/tax/promo in master data causes widespread leakage; mitigated by data-integrity monitoring
- **Unauthorized-change risk**: Manual/unapproved price changes introduce leakage; mitigated by change governance
System Touchpoints: - Master data (links to VS-29); merchandising/pricing (links to VS-01.2); POS/IT (links to VS-08/VS-27); tax (links to VS-79); data quality (links to VS-28.2/W1177); promotions (links to VS-58)

steps.activity: Revenue Assurance Lead/MDM assure pricing/promo master-data integrity: verify price master accuracy (SRP/trade/corporate/promo/bundle/quantity-break per profile §9.3), promo master setup, tax/VAT codes, and mandatory-discount configuration; detect data defects that cause leakage

Revenue Assurance Lead/IT govern pricing/promo system changes: control price-change and promo-setup through approval (links to W3695), test-before-deploy, and audit-trail; prevent unauthorized/manual price changes that cause leakage

Revenue Assurance Lead/MDM monitor master-data quality KPIs (links to VS-28.2/W1177), drive remediation of data defects found via leakage root-cause (W3705), and report master-data integrity to MDM governance (links to VS-29) and program analytics (W3707)

fields.Participants: Revenue Assurance Lead, IT (links to VS-27/VS-113), BI/Data (links to VS-28), POS (links to VS-08), Finance (links to VS-17), Enterprise Architecture (links to VS-113.2), Procurement (links to VS-34)
fields.Trigger: Tooling need; automation opportunity; technology refresh

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "Revenue Assurance Lead/IT maintain the revenue-assurance technology stack" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-detect of "Revenue Assurance Lead/BI develop and tune leakage-detection analytics/models" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-capture of "Revenue Assurance Lead/IT automate revenue-assurance workflows" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-585 (ensure controlled execution — Leakage Recovery, Revenue Analytics & Continuous Assurance (PA-118.3).)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Tooling-gap risk**: Manual/spreadsheet-based assurance misses leakage; mitigated by automation
- **Integration risk**: RA tooling not integrated to source systems; mitigated by architecture alignment
System Touchpoints: - IT operations (links to VS-27); BI/data (links to VS-28); enterprise architecture (links to VS-113.2); POS event stream (links to VS-08); AI/ML (links to VS-30.2); data governance (links to VS-28.2)

steps.activity: Revenue Assurance Lead/IT maintain the revenue-assurance technology stack: exception-monitoring and analytics platform, reconciliation tooling (e.g., BlackLine or custom per W348), POS-event streaming, and the leakage-detection models; ensure integration to POS/ecommerce/payment/GL systems

Revenue Assurance Lead/BI develop and tune leakage-detection analytics/models: anomaly detection on pricing/override/promo/loyalty/refund/catch-weight/payment patterns, threshold rules, and ML-based detection where appropriate (links to VS-30.2); manage false-positive tuning
steps.r: Revenue Assurance Lead / BI / Data Science

steps.activity: Revenue Assurance Lead/IT automate revenue-assurance workflows: automate reconciliation, exception-routing, and reporting; align to enterprise architecture (links to VS-113.2) and data governance (links to VS-28.2); report tooling effectiveness to program governance (links to W3689)

fields.Participants: Revenue Assurance Lead, Cross-Entity Shared Services (links to VS-72), Finance/Consolidation (links to VS-17.2), Digital Commerce entity (links to VS-10), Treasury (links to VS-18), Audit (links to VS-21.3)
fields.Trigger: Multi-entity revenue; consolidated close; group reporting

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-file of "Revenue Assurance Lead/Cross-Entity coordinate revenue assurance across the 5" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-report of "Revenue Assurance Lead/Consolidation consolidate group revenue assurance" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-post of "posture to the audit committee" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-585 (ensure controlled execution — Leakage Recovery, Revenue Analytics & Continuous Assurance (PA-118.3).)
- operational: intercompany reconciliation; operational: consolidation assurance
Pain Points / Risks: - **Entity-misrecognition risk**: Revenue recognized by the wrong entity (e.g., Digital Commerce vs Depot); mitigated by intercompany reconciliation
- **Elimination-error risk**: Intercompany revenue not eliminated in consolidation; mitigated by consolidation assurance
System Touchpoints: - Cross-entity/intercompany (links to VS-72); consolidation (links to VS-17.2); digital commerce (links to VS-10); treasury (links to VS-18); audit (links to VS-21.3); governance (links to VS-36)

steps.activity: Revenue Assurance Lead/Cross-Entity coordinate revenue assurance across the 5 legal entities: confirm revenue is recognized by the correct entity (Depot Inc. recognizes ecommerce revenue at fulfillment per profile §2; Digital Commerce Inc. charges the fulfillment fee), reconcile intercompany revenue/fees (links to VS-72.2), and detect cross-entity leakage

Revenue Assurance Lead/Consolidation consolidate group revenue assurance: ensure the consolidated revenue (links to VS-17.2) is complete and accurate across entities, intercompany revenue is eliminated, and group leakage is quantified and reported

Revenue Assurance Lead/Audit support group/external audit and consolidated revenue-reporting defense (links to VS-21/VS-22/VS-79), and report consolidated revenue-assurance posture to the audit committee (links to VS-21/VS-36) and governance (links to W3689)

fields.Participants: Revenue Assurance Lead, Finance (links to VS-17.4), Audit (links to VS-21.3), BI (links to VS-28.1), Channel owners, Governance (links to VS-36), Risk (links to VS-21.2)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-monitor of "monitoring → predictive/preventive" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-detect of "detective to preventive controls" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-report of "report program maturity, leakage-reduction progress against target, and…" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-585 (ensure controlled execution — Leakage Recovery, Revenue Analytics & Continuous Assurance (PA-118.3).)
- operational: maturity roadmap; operational: continuous-improvement and preventive focus
Pain Points / Risks: - **Maturity-stall risk**: Program stuck at reactive-audit level; mitigated by maturity roadmap
- **Target-miss risk**: Leakage-reduction target not met; mitigated by continuous-improvement and preventive focus
System Touchpoints: - Program governance (links to W3689); audit (links to VS-21.3); BI (links to VS-28.1); governance/board (links to VS-36); risk (links to VS-21.2)

steps.activity: Revenue Assurance Lead assess program maturity against a revenue-assurance maturity model (reactive audit → periodic controls → continuous monitoring → predictive/preventive), identify gaps, and set the maturity-improvement roadmap

Revenue Assurance Lead drive continuous improvement: implement monitoring for newly-mapped leakage vectors (W3690), expand channel coverage, advance analytics/automation (W3710), and mature from detective to preventive controls

Revenue Assurance Lead report program maturity, leakage-reduction progress against target, and residual revenue-leakage exposure to governance (links to W3689/VS-36), the executive risk committee (links to VS-21.2), and the board (links to VS-36)
